label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration, drop-off

Last month Dana asked whether anyone had used Harbor Point, and I said I would write it up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now done eight days of a civil trial, so here is the review, starting with what Ellen's pinned post asks for.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3
Work done: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, internal battery replaced
Dropped off: Monday, October 19
Returned: Tuesday, October 27, which is 6 business days against the 10 quoted
Quoted: $285
Paid: $310 (the extra $25 was the battery, which I approved in advance)
Loaner: yes, a Stenvale Aria 2
Who paid: I did, as I do for all my equipment. No reimbursement from the court.
Warranty: 90 days on the work

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back. Gloria Ruark is the technician and handled my machine from start to finish.

The work is good. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers, and the number bar did not double a single stroke. Nothing in the days since has changed my opinion. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment, which I have never had from anyone.

On price, $310 is fair for what was done. Partway through, Gloria found my battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity. She emailed to say a replacement would be $25 and that she would not go ahead without my approval. That matters to me. I have had invoices from other shops that grew without anyone asking.

The loaner was less happy. The tilt arm would not hold its position and slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, so I spent the rest of the day with it propped on a legal pad. I told Gloria, and she thanked me and said they would repair it before it goes out again. If you take a loaner, set it up at your working angle and lean on it before you leave the shop.

The real weakness is the phone. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. For anyone working a Monday docket, the day you are most likely to discover a problem is a day you cannot reach them. I also called on a Wednesday, inside those hours, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there is no voicemail box to leave a message in. Gloria emailed the following day about the battery, and every email I had from her was prompt and clear, so email is the way to deal with them. But if you are standing in a hallway with a dead machine and want to speak to a person, this is not the shop for that.

Dana, to answer your question: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. Your complaint was the number bar, and that is exactly where mine has been faultless since it came back. They also beat their own estimate by four business days, which should help with your worry about being without it. Go in knowing three things: do your talking by email, do not expect to reach anyone on a Monday or Friday, and check the loaner before you drive away.

I would use them again.

Maureen
